system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: a portable agent skill that encodes the stage ordering and decision rules
system_prompt_style.note: Skill is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter loaded into the host agent's context.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: At each stage, structured artifacts are written so that the next stage, or any external tool, can read what happened in a canonical form rather than parse free-form chat.
env_context_strategy.note: Agent reads working-directory artifacts via tools; no injected file tree described.

observation_format.evidence_quote: expose each stage as a schema-validated tool call rather than as free-form code
observation_format.note: Structured outputs e.g. analysis_results.json read by the agent.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standard way for an agent to call external tools through typed inputs and structured outputs

tool_count.evidence_quote: Each stage is exposed through one tool: a setup tool, a planning tool, an execution tool, and an analysis tool. A fifth tool returns the live set of supported dimensions, shapes, ensembles, tunable parameters, and incompatible mixture rules
tool_count.note: Counts the MCP server tools only; host agent (e.g. Claude Code) adds its own tools.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Each stage is exposed through one tool: a setup tool, a planning tool, an execution tool, and an analysis tool.
edit_primitive.note: No file-editing primitive in the MCP server; host agent supplies editing.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: an MCP tool server exposing each workflow stage as a schema-validated tool

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: autonomously runs Monte Carlo simulations of colloidal packing through a Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool server and an agent skill

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: A colloidal-packing study breaks into four stages, as shown in Fig. 2(a): setup, planning, execution, and analysis.
loop_primitives.note: Skill enforces stage ordering; agent iterates sweeps within it.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: The system can run as a standalone agent or as a tool-and-skill bundle inside existing agent frontends.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The system can run as a standalone agent or as a tool-and-skill bundle inside existing agent frontends.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: The agent advances one workflow stage per turn and waits for explicit user confirmation before invoking each tool.
human_in_loop.note: Interactive mode is per-stage confirmation; autonomous/autoresearch modes run without confirmation.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: During a simulation, the state for a study persists under a single working directory.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: the skill encodes a four-stage workflow contract
long_term_memory.note: Skill = installed reusable procedure; working-directory JSON artifacts persist across runs/iterations.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: each iteration's full data (simulation plan.json, run *directories, analysis results.json) is preserved
state_persistence.note: Artifacts re-read by later stages/iterations; no explicit resume path documented.

self_verification.evidence_quote: The analysis tool runs an automatic equilibrium detection (analyze process time series) and writes an equilibrium block into analysis results.json
self_verification.note: Harness-run automatic equilibration check gating each run; closest value to an automated verifier.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: When a run fails the equilibration check, the agent re-runs that run only with 2-3x more sample steps.
retry_policy.note: Retries until equilibration passes or the absolute sample-steps cap is reached; specified by the autoresearch program file.

rollback.evidence_quote: Each iteration is a fresh setup; prior runs are never overwritten.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: iterating until the goals below are met or until further escalation would exceed the absolute cap
termination_condition.note: Sample-step cap bounds work; benchmark runs short-circuit on off-rail flag.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: tiers the sample steps budget into exploratory (<=5x10 5), refinement (<=2x10 6), and an absolute cap of 5x10 6
cost_controls.note: Compute budget rather than token budget; cost/token usage only measured in benchmark, not enforced.

timeouts.evidence_quote: The simulation execution and analysis tools run asynchronously, so the agent will not time out during the time-consuming simulation process.
timeouts.note: Explicitly designed to avoid tool timeouts.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: The MCP server is implemented as a Python wrapper around the colpack package.
execution_isolation.note: Local MCP server process; no container/VM isolation described.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: During a simulation, the state for a study persists under a single working directory.
filesystem_access.note: Tool artifacts scoped to the working directory; host agent file access unrestricted.

network_policy.evidence_quote: we route all model calls through OpenRouter with the Google Vertex provider selected
network_policy.note: No network restriction described anywhere in the paper.

permission_model.evidence_quote: The agent advances one workflow stage per turn and waits for explicit user confirmation before invoking each tool.
permission_model.note: Default interactive mode; autonomous and autoresearch modes disable confirmation.

tracing.evidence_quote: At each stage, structured artifacts are written so that the next stage, or any external tool, can read what happened in a canonical form
tracing.note: Benchmark also reads flags from a run summary.

replayability.evidence_quote: a program file that frames a colloidal-packing question and a single launch prompt pointing the agent at it
replayability.note: Program file plus preserved artifacts allow re-running a study, not trajectory replay.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: we develop a stage-aware benchmark on top of the same MCP tool stack and run it across a panel of LLMs
eval_hooks.note: 17-prompt benchmark with an eval runner and success flags.

guardrails.evidence_quote: the agent skill checks it before setup, and the setup tool enforces the same rule so that disallowed mixtures are rejected before any simulation is launched

target_domain.evidence_quote: an agent framework that autonomously runs Monte Carlo simulations of colloidal packing

open_source.evidence_quote: The colpack package and corresponding agent skill are available at the GitHub repository https://github.com/ljding94/ColPackAgent.
open_source.note: Public repo; licence not stated in the evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We also compare model performance on this workflow across a panel of LLMs with 17 stage-specific prompts.
model_agnostic.note: Inferred from the paper comparing multiple LLMs, and from the MCP server + skill design usable 'inside an existing agent system'. No LLM client abstraction or dependency line is shown in the excerpts. Repo evidence points to Claude Code (a single-vendor host), so this value is uncertain.

primary_artifact.note: No repository evidence for the ColPackAgent repo itself was supplied; the pinned repo evidence is Claude Code, a host frontend.
